scope: Independent source and offline process review. Hosted game renders and physical-GPU performance remain separate acceptance steps.
admission: Each job owns a single renderer and workload. Every field case executes baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline in one matrix job on the same VM. Normal imports and field captures require clean checked exits. The detail-only runs pair baseline/candidate on one VM. Timings and image differences are compared within a workload.

Before launch, the runner checks the candidate checkout against the exact tracked app/assets scope, hashes runtime files, and verifies the original candidate and baseline shader bytes. It restores the prior bytes in a finally block. Each variant has a fresh environment profile and reimports its native resources. Production hashes listed here match the previously reviewed f066ef26 commit byte-for-byte.

The field runner samples the direct engine process with --resources and a one-second interval; its raw telemetry file and capture ID are matched to the checked verdict. CPU and RSS include engine startup and the selected workload. GPU poll age is unverified; the virtual device cannot establish physical-GPU throughput or target FPS.

The lifecycle helper relays both Godot output streams through EOF to the independent checked runner, identifies the renderer from a bounded copy of the startup header and rejects mismatched or missing expected evidence. This resolves a draft bug that read the buffered and unfinished outer engine log. Final validation waits for the relay to drain. A late engine error still fails the outer checked verdict even after image acceptance.

An image-only lifecycle may request termination after a fully validated expected manifest and PNG set remains unchanged across the 30-second grace. It verifies full PNG structure, full pixel decode, 1920×1080 dimensions, nonuniform content, expected metadata and any supplied native hashes. It records wrapper-issued signals, engine exit and evidence digests, then recomputes the evidence after exit. Ordinary failures, external signals, changed evidence and deadline expiry cannot be promoted to clean completion.

Pair reduction verifies corresponding device and scene inputs before comparing RGB pixels. Camera/clock/material inputs are fixture-specific. The six field views use source-identified camera definitions and readback of the recorded scene configuration. Raw per-run field samples and resource reports are retained. Duplicate repeat-field PNGs may be removed when all RGB values match their same-variant primary; each repeat still has its own PNG and RGB digest. Different repeat images and all first baseline/candidate images are retained.

The two roof close-ups add named-mesh, active material, two-metre distance and UV determinant witnesses from three rays. They guard against the old 1e-6 condition at the targeted centre; actual pixel visibility, foreground occlusion and any improvement must be checked in the resulting frames.

All stdout/stderr remains available. The known optional re-spirv unsupported-opcode message has a dedicated counter; the classification, pinned engine sources and original Forward+ occurrence counts appear in hosted-initial-forward-plus.json. A forced image-only cleanup is independent of whether all engine teardown completed.

independent_nested_process_checks.method: Ran the actual run_checked process around the actual detail helper with a Python child, a short renderer-identification log, and the two archived Forward+ baseline lunar PNGs and manifest in a fresh temporary directory for each case. These synthetic process checks exercise the lifecycle and error plumbing without starting Godot.
